context: Refactors the CSV export loop, described in the PR as cleaning up the row-building logic.
explanation: A new StringBuilder is allocated on every loop iteration just to build one row, and the result is then appended to csv with +=, which reallocates and copies the entire growing string on every iteration. For N rows this is O(N^2) allocation and copying instead of O(N), turning a fast export into a slow one on large datasets and adding significant GC pressure. Fix: use a single StringBuilder created once before the loop (ideally pre-sized with an initial capacity) and append rows to it directly, returning ToString() once at the end.
